title: Platform Operator Credential Rotation and Safe Deployments Guide
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
This guide documents Redwood Inference's recommended patterns and operator procedures for rotating credentials and performing safe platform deployments that depend on secret changes. It consolidates automation recipes, preflight checks, dashboards to monitor, escalation steps, and a retrospective template. The goal is to minimize customer impact, avoid silent failures, and make credential rotation auditable and repeatable.

Scope & Audience
- Scope: platform operator workflows (control plane services, model-serving runtime, inter-service API tokens, K8s service account keys, database credentials, TLS certificates, KMS/HSM integration).
- Audience: platform operators, SREs, infra engineers performing rotations or designing rotation automation, security reviewers.

High-level goals
- Zero-to-low customer-visible interruptions during rotations.
- Short blast radius and fast rollback for bad rotations.
- Complete audit trail and metrics to detect and alert on failures.

Definitions
- Credential: any secret or key material used for authentication/authorization (API tokens, service account keys, DB passwords, TLS certs).
- Rotation: replacing an existing credential with a new value and updating all dependents so the service continues to operate.
- Owner: the service or team responsible for the credential lifecycle.

Risks and mitigations
- Stale clients: ensure dual-write/dual-serve window (old + new active) during rollout.
- Orphaned secrets: automated discovery + periodic inventory reconciliation.
- KMS/HSM errors: circuit-breaker and manual fallback documented.
- Secret spread across regions: coordinate cross-region rollout and include region tags in rotation jobs.

Rotation cadence and policy (recommended)
- Short-lived tokens (API/session tokens): rotate every 24 hours or less if feasible.
- Service account keys: rotate quarterly and immediately on suspected compromise.
- Database credentials: rotate quarterly with automated credential broker.
- TLS certs: renew 30 days before expiry; automatic rolling via cert-manager for K8s workloads.

Credential types and patterns
1) K8s service account tokens / secrets- Pattern: use projected service account tokens or short-lived K8s-bound tokens rather than static secrets.
- Implementation: enable TokenRequest API; adopt token refresh sidecar or kubelet projected tokens.
- Rollout: staged patch of Deployments/StatefulSets to introduce token refresh logic.
2) Long-lived service keys (cloud provider service accounts)
- Pattern: prefer short-lived impersonation tokens where supported; if not, use a key rotation operator that creates keys, updates IAM bindings, and deprecates previous keys.
- Safety: use gradual deprecation with TTL on keys and enforce active-key-list size <= 2.
3) Database credentials
- Pattern: brokered credentials (vault-style) with per-service dynamic credentials.
- Rollout: update connection poolers to handshake new creds without restart (support credential hot-swap).
4) TLS certificates
- Pattern: automated provisioning (ACME/cert-manager) with readiness probes that verify chain and key usage before swap.
5) API tokens and third-party keys
- Pattern: proxy layer for third-party keys so keys can be swapped inside the proxy without changing client configs.

Automated rotation pipeline (recommended architecture)
- Components: rotation-controller (job scheduler), secrets-operator (applies updated secrets to stores), canary-updater (performs canary deploys), verification-worker (runs health checks and smoke tests), audit-logger.
- High-level flow:
  1. Create new credential using authoritative issuer (KMS/Vault/HSM).
  2. Stage credential in a restricted secrets namespace/preview store.
  3. Canary: patch one non-critical instance or a canary deployment to consume the new credential.
  4. Run verification-worker: connectivity tests, smoke requests, telemetry sanity checks.
  5. Promote: update secrets store entries for production, trigger rolling restart or in-place swap depending on service support.
  6. Deprecate old credential: keep for a configurable grace period (default 1 hour) then revoke.

Preflight checklist (must pass before starting rotation)
- Ownership verified: owner_team listed and on-call notified.
- Rollout window reserved and stakeholder notified.
- Backup: export current secret metadata (not plaintext) and audit tokens.
- Health baseline snapshot: current SLI values (latency, error-rate, token-use rate).
- Test playbook available and smoke test scripts validated.

Operator runbook: performing a manual or semi-automated rotation
1. Initiate rotation job in the rotation-controller UI/CLI.
2. Observe canary create: wait for canary pod to become Ready.
3. Run verification-worker job: execute smoke tests (example curl /health, DB test query).
4. If smoke tests pass: kick off staged rollout: patch 20% of replicas, wait 5 minutes, monitor. Repeat with 50% then 100%.
5. If any stage fails: follow rollback path (see Rollback Procedure).
6. After 100% success and 30 minutes of stable metrics, schedule old credential revocation.

Rollback procedure (fast-path)
- Criteria that trigger rollback: >3% error-rate increase OR latency >2x baseline OR failed canary health check.
- Steps:
  1. Pause rotation-controller and mark job as failed.
  2. Reapply old secret value to secrets store.
  3. Trigger controlled restart or in-place swap to revert to old secret where necessary.
  4. Notify owner_team and open an incident if outage occurred.
  5. Collect logs and revert any IAM policy changes (if applicable).

Emergency unrevertable failure path
- If the new credential causes credential store corruption (e.g., malformed key), immediately escalate to security and platform engagement, put affected services into read-only mode (if supported), and execute manual recovery from signed metadata backups.

Verification and observability requirements
- Dashboards (required panels):
  - Rotation job status feed (queued / running / success / failed).
  - Canary health: success/failure counts and last-run snapshot.
  - Secret churn rate by service.
  - Deprecation queue and stale-secret inventory.
  - Error budget impact for rotations (SLO burn caused by rotation operations).

Suggested alerts and thresholds
- Alert: Canary failure — severity P1 if canary fails to reach Ready in 10 minutes.
- Alert: Rollout error spike — P2 when errors increase by >3% above baseline for >5 minutes.
- Alert: Stale secret >90 days and used by active tenants — P3.
- Alert: Unrevoked old key >grace-period+24h — P2 (indicates automation issue).

Metric collection and SLI examples
- SLI: rotation success rate (target >= 99.5% monthly).
- SLI: mean time to rollback (target <= 10 minutes for automated revert).
- SLI: fraction of services using dynamic credentials (target >= 80% by end of Q2 2026).

Ownership, roles, and contact matrix
| Role | Responsibility | Primary owner | Escalation contact |
|------|----------------|---------------|-------------------|
| Rotation-controller ops | Maintain scheduler and job health | platform-ops | oncall-platform@redwood.com |
| Secrets-operator | Keeper of secret-sync logic | infra-sec | infra-sec-lead@redwood.com |
| Service owner | Validate post-rotation health | owning-team | listed in service registry |
| Security reviewer | Approve rotation for high-sensitivity creds | security | security-oncall@redwood.com |
Note: service registry entries must include secret owner and rotation window.

Templates and CLI examples
- rotation-controller CLI (example):
  redwood-rotation create --service model-runtime --credential-type kms-key --canary-replicas 1 --stages 20,50,100 --grace-period 60m
- verification-worker curl test example:
  curl -fS -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /var/run/cred-token)" https://model-runtime.internal/health || exit 1

- Example: Secrets-operator patch (k8s secret, simulated):
  kubectl patch secret svc-model-runtime-creds -p '{"stringData":{"KEY":"<new-value>"}}' -n model-runtime

Retrospective and post-rotation review template
1. Summary: what was rotated, why, owner, times.
2. Outcome: success/failure, metrics affected.
3. Timeline: key events with timestamps.
4. Root cause analysis (if failure).
5. Action items: owners, due dates, verification steps.
6. Lessons learned and documentation updates.

Quarterly roadmap items (recommended)
- Q1 2026: Deploy rotation-controller multi-region replication and MFA-protected promotion approvals.
- Q2 2026: Migrate 60% of long-lived keys to short-lived impersonation tokens.
- Q3 2026: Integrate rotation telemetry with cost and SLA dashboards.
- Q4 2026: Full automatic TLS lifecycle for model-serving fleet.

Appendix A: Verification checklist (operator)
- Canary pod ready and serving health endpoint returns HTTP 200 for 3 consecutive checks.
- Telemetry: no >2x latency spike for 15 minutes.
- Error-rate delta <= 3% over baseline for 10 minutes after each stage.
- At 100% stage validate sample end-to-end customer flows.

Appendix B: Quick decision flow (one-line thumb rules)
- If canary passes: continue staged rollout.
- If canary has intermittent failures: pause, investigate logs and metrics, possibly retry canary with different replica.
- If canary fails consistently: rollback and open incident.

Appendix C: Audit and compliance notes
- All rotations must emit audit events to the centralized audit-logger with job_id, initiator, affected_services, and proofs (signed metadata).
- For restricted credentials (PCI/PHI-scoped): require security reviewer approval and run a test in the restricted sandbox before production promotion.

See Also

Owner and maintenance
- Document owner: platform-ops (Maya Patel). Review cadence: biannual or after any P1 rotation incident.
